analysis.title: Global Healthcare: Pharmaceuticals: Friday Fodder: Tailwinds Persisting
key_insights: Every large-cap biopharma company that has reported 3Q26 so far registered a topline beat, and many also raised topline guidance (Exhibit 1). Stocks were generally rewarded on print day, with BIIB and GSK as exceptions. JNJ sold off on its print but has since more than round-tripped the move.

GS attributes the persisting sector inflows to macro factors (downside economic growth risk benefiting defensives, rotation out of AI/tech) and to micro factors (3Q earnings delivery versus more mixed results elsewhere in healthcare, such as MedTech bellwethers this week).

Healthcare is the second best performing S&P 500 sector ytd, behind only Energy, and large-cap biopharma leads the healthcare subsectors. Pharma now trades at parity with the S&P 500 on forward P/E, versus a 7% discount a week ago and a 27% discount entering the year. Exhibit 2 shows the current reading at +2% against a long-run average of 1%.

GS notes Pharma has traded at a premium to the S&P 500 at times over the last 30 years in backdrops with similar preconditions for multiple expansion, but cautions against over-relying on historical analogs.

LLY is the large-cap name whose multiple has held constant ytd, with estimate revisions driving upside. This week it posted another solid 3Q and a third consecutive guidance raise that comfortably beat expectations. GS acknowledges LLY had a different starting valuation than peers.

Earnings-call themes: M&A appetite (BMY is actively evaluating multiple opportunities, ABBV referenced obesity, MRK called out immunology), cost controls supporting profitability beats (Roche, Novartis, Sanofi), vaccine headwinds (GSK and MRK called out vaccine hesitancy), 340B tailwinds (Novartis, Sanofi), and AI efforts starting to be quantified (BMY).
At ESMO, GS calls out AMGN, JNJ, MRK and MRNA as having the most positive updates (practice-changing data) in its large-cap coverage.

Week ahead: remaining large-cap earnings (AMGN, MRNA, Novo Nordisk, PFE, VRTX, with PFE and MRNA the next read on vaccines) and the US midterm elections. Panelists on a recent GS Washington DC trip saw low likelihood of near-term drug pricing risk, with more policy uncertainty in other parts of healthcare than in large-cap biopharma. Focus is also expected to grow on positioning into clinical catalysts before year-end.
US biotech outperformed this week: XBI +5.53% and NBI +4.35% versus the S&P 500 +1.19%, on interest rate tailwinds, rotation away from AI/tech, and positive earnings and clinical updates.

BIIB reported a top- and bottom-line beat. GS cites subcutaneous Leqembi momentum, Syfovre commercial injection volume +18% YoY, and high-dose Spinraza driving switches. Phase 3 litifilimab data in SLE arrive in 1H December, and GS estimates a ±10-15% stock move if both studies succeed or fail. GS believes post-data weakness would be bought into a strong 2027, and is most constructive on 1H Phase 3 data for litifilimab in CLE and felzartamab in antibody mediated rejection.

ALNY posted a fundamentally in-line 3Q but guided to the lower end of the $4.2-4.5bn FY26 TTR revenue range (GSe $4.287bn). GS sees limited visibility into 2027 and beyond and flags 340B headwinds. ALNY trades near GS's ~$165/share value on flat Amvuttra revenue/OpEx and no pipeline, and GS says greater comfort on the trajectory is needed for a sustained recovery. Phase 2 ALN-6400 (HHT) and Phase 1 ALN-2232 (obesity) data come in February.

GILD beat on top and bottom line. GS focuses on diversification beyond HIV: anito-cel in 4L+ multiple myeloma (Dec 23 PDUFA), the Trodelvy collaboration with BNTX, and I&I programs including edecesertib (IRAK4) Phase 2a data in CLE at ACR on Nov 8. REGN's topline beat was driven by increased Eylea HD demand and GS finds the valuation attractive. INCY raised FY26 guidance, with mCALR 1L myelofibrosis data at ASH (Dec 12-15) the key pipeline driver.

AMGN's Phase 3 DeLLphi-305 data for Imdelltra in 1L maintenance ES-SCLC drew a standing ovation and was published in NEJM. GS believes the data and KOL feedback support Imdelltra as standard of care in 1L maintenance. Positive readthrough to Phase 3 DeLLphi-312 in 1L induction would unlock ~23K US patients versus ~14K addressable in 2L+.

MRNA/MRK's intismeran plus Keytruda cut recurrence in adjuvant melanoma versus Keytruda alone (RFS HR=0.58, p<0.001), meeting the <0.60 bar, with a post-6-month HR of 0.42. Early PDAC data showed 11/20 ongoing responses in an immunotherapy-refractory setting. Next focus is RCC data in late-26/2027.

SMMT's partner Akeso presented Phase 3 HARMONi-GI1 (China-only) in frontline biliary tract cancer: ivonescimab plus chemotherapy beat Imfinzi plus chemotherapy (OS HR=0.75, p=0.0031), the first Phase 3 win beyond NSCLC. The global HARMONi-3 frontline NSCLC study reads out by YE/early-27, and investors expect a PFS HR of 0.72 or better, while GS says a statistically significant PFS (HR<0.80) and an OS trend would support approval.

Near-term biotech catalysts: ASH abstracts release Nov 4, ACR meeting Nov 6-11 (AMGN anti-CD40L in Sjögren's, CRSP zugo-cel in systemic sclerosis, ALLO-329), GILD IRAK4 CLE data Nov 8 and anito-cel PDUFA Dec 23, BIIB SLE Phase 3 in 1H December, ANNX Phase 3 geographic atrophy data (potential Syfovre competitor), SMMT HARMONi-3 squamous cohort in 2H, and FDA approval for REGN's cemdisiran in generalized myasthenia gravis.

EU Pharma: 3Q26 is another beat-and-raise quarter, helped by one-time items (revenue pull-forward, gross-to-net benefits) and flat OpEx. The SXDP is up c.14% in the past month on multiple expansion and EU Pharma is up c.9%, while guidance-driven earnings upgrades imply only c.1-2% upside on average so far.

EU results detail: Roche sales beat consensus by 2%, or 1% excluding a Japan pull-forward ahead of an ERP switchover. Novartis sales were in line but cost control drove an 8%/7% operating profit/EPS beat and a profitability guidance raise, with the long-term debate on post-2030 growth versus patent expirations unresolved. Sanofi beat by 26% on earnings with new guidance implying c.5% upside to consensus, and Dupixent volumes in the US are growing 17/18%, which could make the €25bn 2030 peak sales guidance look conservative.

Next week Bayer and Novo report. GS believes consensus mis-models Bayer's CropScience seasonality. For Novo, consensus expects strong Wegovy pill sales and a guidance upgrade, and Sanofi's read-across suggests 340B gross-to-net adjustments could support Novo's insulin franchise, which consensus does not currently model. Bayer is back at/above €50 after positive Nubeqa prostate data and a win in the Aretino glyphosate case, and approval of the proposed class settlement could allow a breakout above €50.

Obesity script watch: overall GLP-1 obesity scripts rose c.4% w-o-w, breaching 1.4m weekly per IQVIA. Wegovy pill TRx rose c.6% to 183k, near its high. Foundayo TRx rose c.9% to 63.1k, with TRx share at 26% (17% at the start of summer) and NBRx share at 37%. Pen TRx share is 33:67 Wegovy versus Zepbound, shifting toward Zepbound since July, and total market share including orals is 36:64, with NBRx share at 39:61 in Lilly's favor.

AZN and GSK both reported core EPS beats of similar magnitude, but stock reactions diverged on perceived 2027 outlook. GSK faces a quiet catalyst path and HIV pipeline concerns, while AZN's lack of cautious 2027 opex commentary was received positively. GMAB has delivered on all three binary catalysts, with petosemtamab positive in head and neck cancer, and the stock is up more than 100% in three months. ARGX's EMPASSION readout for empasiprubart is the key remaining high-profile clinical readout into year-end.

Generic pharma is up 37% ytd on a market-cap weighted basis, versus XLV +16% and the S&P 500 +13%. GS sees an attractive setup into YE26+. TEVA and VTRS are expected to report in-line quarters next week, and AMRX has potential for a beat-and-raise.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 large-cap biopharma, reported: all 12 companies in Exhibit 1 posted a topline beat versus consensus (REGN and AZN 10/30, LLY 10/29, GILD 10/29 post close, MRK 10/29, ABBV 10/30, SNY 10/30, BMY 10/29, NVS 10/27, BIIB 10/28, GSK 10/28, JNJ 10/13). Topline guidance was raised by LLY, GILD, MRK, ABBV, SNY, BMY and JNJ and reiterated by AZN, NVS, BIIB and GSK.

LLY reported 3Q26 on 10/29 with its third consecutive guidance raise. Post-earnings revisions in Exhibit 1: 2026 sales +1.8%, 2027 sales +2.3%, 2026 EPS +4.1%, 2027 EPS +4.1%. Exhibit 1 also shows JNJ 2027 EPS revisions at -6.2%.
Roche reported 3Q26 sales only: +2% above consensus, or +1% excluding a Japan pull-forward ahead of an ERP system switchover.
Novartis reported 3Q26 sales in line with consensus, with an 8% operating profit beat and a 7% EPS beat on SG&A and R&D cost control, and raised profitability guidance.
Sanofi reported 3Q26 sales and Business EPS well above consensus, a 26% earnings beat aided by 340B conversions and cost control. New guidance implies c.5% upside risk to consensus estimates.
AZN and GSK both reported 3Q26 core EPS beats of similar magnitude. Stock reactions diverged on perceived 2027 outlook, with GSK down and AZN up on print day.
ALNY reported an in-line 3Q26 and guided FY26 TTR revenue to the lower end of its $4.2-4.5bn range, versus GS estimate of $4.287bn.
BIIB, GILD and REGN reported 3Q26 top-line beats (BIIB and GILD also beat on the bottom line). INCY raised FY26 guidance.
EU Pharma 3Q26 so far: earnings upgrades from guidance updates imply only c.1-2% upside on average. Only Novo remains to report, expected next week.

Upcoming, consensus or GS expectations only: Novo consensus anticipates strong Wegovy pill sales and a guidance upgrade. Bayer is expected by GS to beat on CropScience seasonality that consensus mis-models. TEVA and VTRS are expected to be in line, and AMRX has potential for a beat-and-raise. AMGN, MRNA, PFE and VRTX also report next week.
risk_factors: Historical premium analogs for Pharma may not hold, and GS cautions against over-relying on them as the multiple reaches parity with the S&P 500.
Vaccine hesitancy flagged by GSK and MRK as an ongoing headwind, with PFE and MRNA results next week as the next read.
ALNY has limited visibility into 2027 and beyond, 340B headwinds and flat Amvuttra revenue.
Binary clinical readouts: BIIB litifilimab SLE (±10-15% stock move), SMMT HARMONi-3 against high PFS expectations, ARGX EMPASSION.
Novartis faces a long-term growth debate versus significant patent expirations, and Roche's giredestrant carries rising expectations and competitor data headline risk.
GSK has launch execution risk, a quiet catalyst path and HIV pipeline concerns.
Revenue beats are partly supported by one-time items (pull-forwards, gross-to-net benefits, 340B conversions) rather than underlying growth.
Policy uncertainty ahead of the US midterms, which GS sees as greater in non-biopharma parts of healthcare.
Bayer glyphosate litigation overhang pending the class settlement approval decision.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 table covers 12 global large-cap biopharma names (REGN, AZN, LLY, GILD, MRK, ABBV, SNY, BMY, NVS, BIIB, GSK, JNJ) with report date, topline beat or raise, day-1 and follow-through absolute and relative performance in bps, and post-earnings revisions to 2026/2027 sales and EPS. The mean is +236bps abs. on day 1 and +478bps including follow-through.
Exhibit 2 plots US large-cap biopharma FY2 P/E discount (equal weighted) versus the S&P 500, with current +2%, 75th percentile 16%, average 1% and 25th percentile -16%.
Exhibit 3 plots ytd relative performance of XLV, the S&P 500 and US Pharma from 12/31/2025 to late October 2026.
vol_and_positioning: Sector inflows into large-cap biopharma are persisting from macro tailwinds (defensive rotation, rotation from AI/tech) and micro earnings delivery.

Pharma forward P/E versus the S&P 500 is at parity, versus a 7% discount a week ago and a 27% discount entering the year. Exhibit 2 shows +2% current against a 75th percentile of 16%, an average of 1% and a 25th percentile of -16%.
Generic pharma is up 37% ytd (market-cap weighted), against XLV +16% and the S&P 500 +13%.
GS estimates BIIB could move ±10-15% on Phase 3 litifilimab SLE results if both studies succeed or fail.
Positioning into key clinical catalysts before year-end is expected to draw growing focus, including SMMT HARMONi-3, BIIB SLE, ARGX EMPASSION and the ACR and ASH meetings.
Bayer shares have treated €50 as a ceiling this year, and approval of the proposed settlement could allow a breakout above it.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: panelists on GS's recent Washington DC trip highlighted a low likelihood of near-term drug pricing risk, with greater policy-related uncertainty in other parts of healthcare than in large-cap biopharma.
340B policy: cited as a tailwind on Novartis and Sanofi earnings calls and a headwind for ALNY's TTR demand.
Medicare IRA implementation: TEVA's Austedo stocking dynamics ahead of implementation are a focus for next week's print.
China volume-based procurement is a focus item for VTRS's global segments.
Medicare BRIDGE programme: LLY management commentary that it is biased toward injectables, with LLY products taking the majority share.
